transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Amy Chen (Redwood AE), Sam Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Miles (Acadia Procurement), Priya Kapoor (Acadia Legal), Ethan Reed (Acadia Security), Maya Ortiz (Acadia Eng)

Summary: quick procurement/contract call to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SLAs (uptime and incident MTTR), pricing approval and vendor onboarding steps. legal has a few redlines around data residency, subprocessor list, and indemnity. Security asked about SOC2, KMS, and private deployment options. Redwood committed to send redlines and security artifacts; next legal touchpoint planned for next week.

Topics: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA targets (99.9 vs 99.95), data residency & on-prem options, pricing & committed usage discounts, procurement timeline, security artifacts (SOC2, pen test), onboarding plan and pilot date.

Transcript:
00:00 Amy: hey everyone thanks for taking time, uh this is Amy from Redwood - i'll kick off - we have Sam the SE here as well. Jordan, Priya, Ethan, Maya, we see you, thanks for joining.
00:12 Jordan: thanks Amy, yeah appreciate it. we're on a bit of a compressed timeline; procurement wants vendor terms and pricing locked by mid april, ideally before our board review.
00:20 Amy: great, yeah we can aim for that - today's goal is to run through the MSA/DPA asks, SLA targets you need, any security docs we should attach, and align on the procurement / PO timeline.
00:29 Priya: hi - i reviewed the MSA and DPA that you sent, there are three legal spots we need to discuss: indemnity cap, data residency clause for PHI, and subprocessor notification timing.
00:40 Sam: priya, can you clarify the residency ask? are you expecting all PHI to live in a us-only region or on-prem?
00:47 Priya: we prefer US-only cloud region for now, but we'll need an option to go on-prem or VPC-hosted in the future for certain regulated services.
00:55 Ethan: and from security, we need to confirm encryption at rest with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and the availability of audit logs for all request/response payloads. also want to see SOC2 type II and a recent pentest.
01:07 Sam: ok yep we have SOC2 Type II and a pen test summary; we can share those. we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and full at-rest encryption on Hosted with redwood-managed keys. for hosted you can also bring your own KMS via our KMS integration.
01:24 Maya: just to add from eng - latency matters for our triage flows. if we go hosted with regional restrictions, we need low ms latencies; what's the SLA and dedicated capacity option?
01:36 Amy: good q. our Dedicated offering gives reserved GPU pools with committed throughput and an SLA. for hosted we publish performance profiles; for your kind of load we usually recommend dedicated if latency under 200ms p95 is required. SLA options - typically 99.9% for hosted, 99.95% for dedicated/committed contracts.
01:55 Jordan: that 99.9 vs 99.95 difference matters - procurement will push for 99.95. what's the penalty/credit structure on SLA breaches?
02:04 Amy: standard credits: for each 30-day period if we miss the SLA, we provide service credits computed as x% of monthly bill up to a cap. We can include a commercial SLA in the SOW with specific credit tiers; legal has asked often to see exact wording so we'll map that into the MSA/SLA appendix.
02:20 Priya: on indemnity, current cap in the MSA is six million, we need to reduce / align with our vendor policy - what's your flexibility?
02:28 Amy: we can escalate; typical enterprise redlines are possible depending on spend and insurance. we may need to route to finance and our legal ops for approval - can you give a target cap?
02:36 Priya: target is 1.5M with carveouts for gross negligence.
02:42 Amy: understood, we'll flag that as a redline.
02:46 Ethan: one technical note: you mentioned cacheing previously - we need clarity on retention of request context and how long KV cache persists for model inference requests if we enable prefix caching. anything stored on our side needs to be covered by DPA.
02:58 Sam: yes, good note. our KV/prefix caching is configurable and can be disabled; default is ephemeral in memory except when customers opt into persistent caching for performance. persistent caches are encrypted and fall under the DPA terms; we'll map the retention options in the DPA.
03:15 Jordan: pricing - we got a ballpark price earlier but procurement needs committed volume discounts and a pricing table for PO. can we get committed tiers?
03:25 Amy: absolutely - we typically offer 10% off list at small commits, and two-tier deeper discounts for 3-12 month reserved commits; for Dedicated we give a capacity price with commit pricing and overage rates. i'll send a pricing summary with three options: hosted pay-as-you-go, 6-12 month committed hosted discount, and Dedicated reserved capacity.
03:40 Maya: and onboarding - what's the typical ramp for us to be able to start pilot in prod? we want a pilot with about 20k requests/day to start.
03:48 Sam: for a pilot we can do a self-serve onboarding plus an assisted kick-off; typical time-to-first-request is days for hosted, and 2-4 weeks if you need VPC or dedicated infra. for dedicated on-prem it's longer due to provisioning.
03:59 Priya: procurement also needs to know standard invoicing terms and PO process; we prefer net 45 but can accept net 30 for first year.
04:08 Jordan: timeline reminder: procurement sign-off by mid april, legal review next week, exec review 2026-04-18.
04:15 Amy: ok let's walk the immediate asks and owners: legal redlines, security docs, pricing PO template, pilot timeline. we'll confirm specific due dates.

04:30 [15m silence while shared doc is pulled up, some cross talk] 
04:45 Sam: i'm pulling the DPA now - note on subprocessors: we notify customers 30 days prior to adding new subprocessors; legal asked for 10 days, we can try to shorten notification but some subprocessors are core infra.
04:58 Priya: 30 days is fine as long as we have the right to object and review data flows - can you commit to a 10-business-day objection window?
05:07 Amy: we can add a clause for a 10-business-day review/objection window for new subprocessors, subject to our ability to ensure continuity of service; we'll draft language.
05:15 Ethan: also - incident response. we need an agreeement on notification for security incidents involving PHI within 24 hours, and a defined SRR (security response runbook) for triage.
05:26 Sam: we have an incident response process and can commit to notifying customers within 24 hours for confirmed incidents affecting PHI; the SRR can be shared under NDA or as redacted version in the security pack.
05:38 Maya: small question - can we pin model versions during the pilot? we want deterministic outputs for regressions.
05:44 Sam: yes you can pin model versions and we support rollouts/canaries. there is also an option to pin quantization profiles for consistency.
05:52 Jordan: about on-prem option - if we opt for private deployment later, how would that affect SLA and pricing?
06:00 Amy: Private deployments have a different pricing model - one-time onboarding + recurring license/infra fee; SLA is typically higher since infra is customer-controlled, we offer support tiers. we'll include a comparison table in the pricing doc.
06:11 Priya: legal nit - will you accept mutual indemnification for third-party claims? the current draft was Redwood indemnifying Acadia for Redwood product defects, but mutual is preferred.
06:21 Amy: mutual indemnity is a common ask; we'll flag and see where we can be reciprocal, though exceptions apply for open-source third-party claims.
06:28 Jordan: procurement will need the final pricing sheet and a PO template to prepare the PO for finance.
06:33 Amy: i'll send that in the follow-up. also i'll include a short statement about our insurance limits.
06:40 Ethan: any concerns about data egress costs? if we keep everything US-only region and we have large volumes, egress could be material - do you have a model for egress billing?
06:50 Amy: egress is billed for Dedicated when we route across regions; for Hosted we try to minimize and typically included for normal API usage within region. we'll call out egress rules in the pricing doc.
06:59 [brief crosstalk - someone drops a link to the MSA in chat] 
07:10 Priya: ok can we summarize agreed immediate next steps?
07:15 Amy: yep - summary: 1) Amy will produce redlined version of MSA + DPA with notes on indemnity, subprocessors, data residency and SLA appendix. 2) Sam will send SOC2 Type II report, pen test summary, and network diagram. 3) Amy will send pricing summary with committed tiers and PO template. 4) Maya will share expected monthly token/request volumes and data residency details. 5) schedule legal follow-up next week (Priya + Amy).
07:40 Jordan: that works. procurement target mid april - we'll work to get PO ready when we get pricing.
07:46 Priya: legal will aim to review redlines within 48-72 hours of receiving them.
07:52 Amy: perfect - we'll aim to get the artifacts by 2026-03-31. would you like us to run a short pilot performance test for the latency-sensitive path?
08:01 Maya: yes pls, that'd be helpful. we can provide a sample dataset and expected qps.
08:07 Sam: cool - i'll coordinate offline with Maya on the pilot test and run a mini-benchmark.
08:12 Jordan: anything else?
08:15 Priya: just one last ask - please include support SLAs for response times and P1/P2 definitions in the appendix.
08:22 Amy: will do.
08:25 Jordan: ok thanks everyone, we'll wait for the package and follow-up invite.
08:29 Amy: thanks all - talk soon.

End of call.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "cacheing" spelled various ways, "Redwood Dedcicated" typo in notes, and speaker overlaps at minute marks. The transcript has been lightly cleaned but retains natural pauses and filler.
